issues.legal_issue: An enforcement auction may be set aside when the secured creditor conducts it with undue haste while related proceedings are pending and material irregularities in the sale are concurrently found.
material_facts: The borrowers had challenged enforcement steps before the tribunal, and proceedings were also pending before the High Court when the bank proceeded with the auction and confirmed the sale.
The tribunal and the High Court both found material irregularities in conducting the auction.
The Supreme Court found that the bank had acted with undue haste and saw no reason to disturb those concurrent findings.
issues.conclusion: The concurrent findings of material irregularities were upheld, and the auction sale remained set aside.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the statutory framework for enforcement of security interests under the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 and the Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002, and declined to disturb concurrent factual findings of material irregularity. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

predicates.appeal_from_order_setting_aside_enforcem: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an order that set aside an enforcement auction.
predicates.sale_held_while_related_proceedings_pend: The secured creditor held the auction while proceedings concerning the enforcement measures were pending.
predicates.bank_acted_with_undue_haste: The secured creditor proceeded with the auction hastily despite the pending proceedings.
predicates.concurrent_findings_of_material_sale_irr: The lower tribunals or courts concurrently found material irregularities in the conduct of the auction.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges the setting aside of an enforcement auction, and the sale took place during pending related proceedings with undue haste and concurrent findings of material irregularity, the auction remains set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A later application challenging enforcement measures is maintainable when it arises from a distinct cause of action created by a completed auction.
material_facts: An earlier application challenged the demand and sale notices before the auction took place.
After the bank held the auction, the borrowers filed a further application challenging the demand notice and the completed sale.
The later application therefore arose from a cause of action different from that of the earlier application.
issues.conclusion: The later application was maintainable because it was based on a different cause of action.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 17(1) of the Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002, a later application is maintainable where its cause of action differs from that raised in an earlier application. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

predicates.application_for_review_of_enforcement_me: The proceeding is an application seeking review of measures taken to enforce a security interest.
predicates.earlier_application_challenged_pre_aucti: An earlier application challenged enforcement steps before the auction had taken place.
predicates.later_application_followed_completed_auc: A later application was filed after the auction had been completed and challenged that sale.

issues.definition: When an application seeks review of enforcement measures, an earlier application challenged pre-auction steps, and a later application follows a completed auction, the later application is maintainable.

issues.legal_issue: Equitable relief may protect an auction purchaser through repayment with interest while allowing a fresh sale subject to notice and an opportunity for the borrowers to pay the dues.
material_facts: The auction purchaser had paid the purchase price for the property.
The sale was set aside because of irregularities in the auction.
The bank was prepared to accept the borrowers’ outstanding dues and return the purchaser’s money with interest.

The Court directed repayment to the purchaser with simple interest and allowed the bank to proceed with a fresh auction if the borrowers failed to pay after being informed of the total dues, subject to public notice.
issues.conclusion: The bank was directed to refund the auction purchaser’s payment with simple interest, and could conduct a fresh auction if the borrowers did not pay the communicated dues, after giving public notice of the sale.
issues.legal_principle: The Court exercised its power under Article 142 of the Constitution of India to shape consequential relief, ordering repayment with interest and permitting a fresh auction on the stated conditions. No earlier cases were relied on for this issue.

predicates.appeal_involving_set_aside_enforcement_s: The proceeding is an appeal involving an enforcement sale that has been set aside.
predicates.purchaser_paid_purchase_price: The auction purchaser paid the purchase price for the property.
predicates.sale_set_aside_for_irregularities: The sale was set aside because of irregularities in conducting the auction.
predicates.borrowers_fail_to_pay_after_bank_communi: The borrowers do not pay the total dues after the secured creditor informs them of the amount payable.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a sale set aside for irregularities after the purchaser paid the price, and the borrowers fail to pay after the dues are communicated, the purchaser is refunded with interest and a fresh sale is conditionally permitted.
